slides.title: Inside DUP Protocol
slides.subtitle: Living architecture of an honest ledger: Python orchestrates, Rust drives the core
slides.voice_text: Welcome inside DUP Protocol. Forget static slides. Let us watch a Layer 1 blockchain come alive like a cosmic engine, where every transaction flies as a beam of light, a red fail-closed shield deflects errors at the perimeter, and every accepted record is sealed forever into the ledger.

slides.title: The Entire Protocol as One Organism
slides.subtitle: Left: ingress and strict filtering · Center: crypto reactor · Right: accounting and mesh sync
slides.voice_text: Look at the whole protocol running in harmony. On the left, transaction streams enter through the API and immediately meet the red fail-closed shield. Any invalid signature or spam bounces off the perimeter. Valid requests flow into the golden Rust mempool and straight into the central crypto reactor powered by abs native and Rocks DB. On the right, accounting updates balances strictly in integer satoshis, consensus locks the canonical chain, and three mesh nodes broadcast the sealed block over encrypted channels.

slides.title: Five Layers, Zero Silent Loss
slides.subtitle: Dimensional boundaries of the architecture: every color represents a distinct class of guarantees
slides.voice_text: How does this ledger record every change cleanly without losing a single byte? Data flows strictly top to bottom through explicit ports. The cyan layer admits signed requests. Violet Python orchestration holds consensus rules and secrets policy. The red network and mempool shield drops spam and forgeries. The emerald execution layer computes integer satoshi balances. And the golden abs native and Rocks DB foundation seals the page to disk.

slides.title: Anatomy of One Transaction
slides.subtitle: From a cyan signature pulse through the red filter and golden Merkle tree to the emerald block seal
slides.voice_text: Let us trace a single transaction beam from start to finish. First, the sender signs a transfer in exact satoshis. Next, the red Rust mempool filter blocks spam, replay nonces, and insufficient balances. Then the golden crypto core folds valid transactions into a Merkle tree and state root. Finally, the new block locks onto the previous hash, snaps shut with an emerald seal, and commits atomically to Rocks DB.

steps.title: Signature
steps.detail: Cyan pulse: integer satoshi amount plus cryptographic signature.

steps.title: Red Filter
steps.detail: Rust mempool rejects spam, duplicate nonces, and low balance.

steps.title: Merkle Tree
steps.detail: Golden SHA-256 folds every transaction into one verifiable root.

steps.title: Chain Link
steps.detail: New block anchors to the previous hash so history cannot be forged.

steps.title: Emerald Seal
steps.detail: Atomic disk commit stitches the page into the ledger forever.

slides.title: Three Nodes in One Pulse
slides.subtitle: Encrypted rust-libp2p Noise channels, emerald live probes, and red fail-closed stop on divergence
slides.voice_text: Immediately after sealing, the new block ripples across the three-node mesh over encrypted Rust libp2p Noise channels. Peers exchange live probes to verify both block height and matching state roots. If a node lags behind, CatchUp and ForkReconcile pull missing headers and verify every link. And if state ever diverges, a red fail-closed stop withdraws readiness instead of painting a false green light.

recovery_steps.title: Red Stop on Failure
recovery_steps.desc: Peer loss or state mismatch withdraws readiness fail-closed — health status never lies.

slides.voice_text: At the heart of speed and determinism sits the real abs native Rust crate. Critical cryptography, state root computation, and Rocks DB persistence execute natively in Rust, while Python remains a clean, readable orchestrator above it.

Zero hard fails across runs and zero floating-point arithmetic in money. Three nodes in the production profile, and two clear repositories: the audit-freeze pin and the experimental lab.
